etymologies.etymologyHTML: From listen +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: Someone who listens, especially to a speech or a broadcast.

quote.citation: 1904, William Henry Hudson, “chapter 2”, in Green Mansions:
quote.text: […]  she would set herself going, telling the most interminable stories, until the last listener was fast asleep […]

quote.citation: 1937, John Steinbeck, Of Mice and Men:
quote.text: And then her words tumbled out in a passion of communication, as though she hurried before her listener could be taken away.

definitions.definition: (computing, programming, chiefly Java) A function that runs in response to an event; an event handler.

quote.citation: Fancy Gazette, quoted in 1823, John Badcock, Slang, a Dictionary of the Turf, the Ring, the Chase, the Pit, of Bon-Ton, and the Varieties of Life
quote.text: Gas now planted his favourite hit under the left listener of his antagonist, which sent him to dorse.
